references.text: Parallel legislation concerning the Feast of Tabernacles, which also sets the fifteenth day of the seventh month as the beginning of a seven-day festival for the Lord.
Moses repeats the command to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days, emphasizing joy before the Lord.
Further provisions regarding the Feast of Tabernacles explaining why the Israelites were to live in booths for seven days.
Ezra mentions the celebration of the Feast of Tabernacles after returning from exile, in accordance with what was prescribed.
Nehemiah describes how the people celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days following the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
The prophecy that all nations will come to Jerusalem to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles in the messianic age.
John notes that the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was near, showing that this festival was still being celebrated during Jesus' time.
Jesus speaks on the last and great day of the Feast of Tabernacles and offers living water to those who thirst.
Solomon gathered Israel in the seventh month for the dedication of the temple, which coincided with the Feast of Tabernacles.
Solomon celebrated the festival for seven days together with all Israel at the temple dedication.
